questionText: Which of the following statement is not true about mahajanapadas of the sixth-century BCE:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
options.mistakeAnalysis: Erroneously assumed both statements were valid.

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
options.mistakeAnalysis: Rejected valid scientific statements erroneously.

options.text: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
options.mistakeAnalysis: Failed to recognize the fallacy in Statement II.

options.text: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Statement I is false while Statement II is factually sound.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
The sixth century BCE is regarded as a major turning point in early Indian history, marked by the emergence of sixteen major territorial states called mahajanapadas. Buddhist and Jaina texts list sixteen states (such as Magadha, Kosala, Vatsa, and Avanti). While most were monarchies ruled by rajas, some were oligarchies known as ganas or sanghas (like the Vajji sangha). Each had a fortified capital city, and rulers maintained standing armies and administrative bureaucracies. Stating that texts mention twenty states is factually incorrect.
Hence, option (D) is correct.

Epigraphic terms: 'Piyadassi' (pleasant to behold) was the standard honorific title used by Emperor Asoka in his rock and pillar edicts (A-(III)). Kalinga was the ancient name for coastal Odisha conquered in Ashoka's eighth regnal year (B-(IV)). Kharosthi was the right-to-left script used for Ashokan edicts in the northwest (C-(I)). In Major Rock Edict VI, Ashoka commanded the 'pativedakas' (special reporters) to report public affairs to him at all times and places (D-(II)). Match: (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(II).
Hence, option (C) is the correct match.
